lesson_text: Both halves matter. The 500% came off just $0.01 a year earlier, so a gain of a few cents reads as a huge percent. Investopedia notes growth rates ignore the amounts involved. Palantir's Q1 report was its sixth straight GAAP-profitable quarter, so this is steady profit, not a one-off. Adjusted EPS grew 80% and revenue grew 27% the same quarter, so the story rests on more than one cent. A huge percent off a tiny base is inflated. Real, growing profit is the real news.

depth.summary: Beating estimates is the norm: on FactSet's 5-year average, 78% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS estimates. Over five years, S&P 500 companies that beat gained 0.9% on average in that window. Over five years, S&P 500 companies that missed lost 3.1% on average in that window. A beat means actual earnings or revenue came in above the consensus estimate; a miss means below it. A company can beat estimates and still fall if its outlook disappoints. prompt_json.q: Two numbers, one verdict
steps: Every quarter has two sides. The company's own numbers usually come in a press release, filed with an 8-K.
The other side is the consensus: the average of the analysts' estimates.
Above the consensus is a beat. Below is a miss. Equal is in line.
Then work the surprise: actual minus consensus, divided by the consensus, times 100.
